title: No merits of the saints, yet the godly may draw God's favor on the whole body
source_text: L. Nolunt quoque bona quae nobis obtingunt Sanctorum meritis tribui, & per eorum merita quicquam a Deo postulari: quia Sancti, qui totum quod erant gratiae divinae debebant, nec sibi, nec aliis quicquam proprie loquendo, mereri potuerunt. Neque tamen propterea negant, vi communionis Sanctorum fieri, ut bona & pia opera, quae a singulis Ecclesiae membris per Dei gratiam fiunt, benedictionem & favorem Dei, in totum corpus quodammodo provocent, atque alliciant: imo quandoque Deum, hominum piorum & justorum intuitu, impiis ipsis, quibus immixti sunt, parcere, & tempus ac media poenitentiam agendi concedere: quemadmodum Dominus Abrahamo professus est se parciturum fuisse Sodomae ipsi & Gomorrhae, si in ea vel decem homines justi reperti fuissent.
pass_a_gloss: They also will not have the good things which befall us attributed to the merits of the Saints, and anything requested from God through their merits: because the Saints, who owed the whole of what they were to divine grace, could merit nothing, properly speaking, either for themselves or for others. Nor yet on that account do they deny that it happens by force of the communion of the Saints, that the good and pious works which are done by individual members of the Church through the grace of God, in some way call forth and attract the blessing and favor of God upon the whole body: indeed that sometimes God, in regard to pious and just men, spares the impious themselves, with whom they are mixed, and grants time and means of doing penitence: just as the Lord professed to Abraham that he would have spared Sodom itself and Gomorrah, if even ten just men had been found in it.
pass_b_english: The Reformed also refuse to credit the good things that come to us to the merits of the saints, or to ask anything of God through their merits. The saints owed all that they were to divine grace, and so, strictly speaking, they could merit nothing either for themselves or for others.

Yet they do not therefore deny that, by virtue of the communion of saints, the good and godly works that individual members of the Church do by God's grace in some way call down and draw God's blessing and favor on the whole body. Indeed, God sometimes spares the ungodly themselves for the sake of the godly and righteous who live among them, and gives them time and means to repent, just as the Lord declared to Abraham that he would have spared Sodom and Gomorrah if even ten righteous people had been found there.

lemmas.gloss: by force of the communion of the Saints

choices.why: God's regard for the righteous is a reason for sparing, not a merit paid; 'for the sake of' keeps that sense.
